column3: The Hebrew repeats the root for taking possession; BSB distinguishes “conquer” and “possess.” It says “before you,” rather than “over to you.”
The Hebrew says “all his people”; BSB interprets this as “his whole army.”
The Hebrew says “before us” and “all his people”; BSB has “over to us” and “his whole army.”
The Hebrew separately names the men and has singular “a survivor”; BSB uses “people” and plural “survivors.”
The Hebrew describes a city being too high, without a separate word for walls. It says that the LORD gave everything “before us.”
The Hebrew verb is “commanded,” without an explicit negative; BSB interprets the contextual restriction as “had forbidden.”
